post.instagram:
Send this to the parent whose child is nine and whose sixteenth birthday feels a long way off.

At sixteen, a child gets the lot. At nine, they get very little. In between, most families have nothing to hold on to, and nobody says what the middle is meant to look like.

A sixteenth birthday is not a training course.

So we made the passport. Five stages, from 4 to 16: calm screen offs, healthy habits, knows how it works, owns their footprint, ready for the world. Each stage earns a stamp, and the stamps fill in from the jobs, the lessons and the check ins you are already doing. It is not a quiz.

It is our answer to that gap, built to be something a family can use on a Tuesday.

Which means the stage your child is at tonight has a job, and you can see it.

So that the words are ready: "You do not get everything at sixteen. You get a little more each time you show me you are ready, and we work out the next step together."

What is the one thing your child could do now that they could not do a year ago?

What stage is your child? Three questions, no sign up, link in bio.
